_notes: Session 2026-09-22, node 1 only, single position. window_std/activity
definitions and the frame_diff/drift dead ends are documented in
server/state.py. The three passes below used std(window_std) computed
over the FULL 45s capture (one number per pass) -- that is NOT the same
quantity as the live `activity` metric, which is std(window_std) over a
rolling ~1s window recomputed every frame. The live metric runs at a
smaller scale for the same reason a short clip has less variance than a
long one. EMPTY_MAX/MOVING_MIN were first set from these 45s numbers,
then MOVING_MIN was corrected (1.0 -> 0.5) after a live test showed the
original value never triggered presence during real movement.
Live-validated 2026-09-22 with MOVING_MIN=0.5: presence correctly
flipped true within ~0.8s of movement onset, dropped back within ~1.2s
of stopping, and stayed pinned at motion=1.0 (comfortable margin above
threshold) throughout sustained movement. See conversation for the
raw timestamped log.
TODO next calibration: capture `activity` (not window_std) stats
directly, at the same ~1s rolling scale the live scorer uses, so the
calibration numbers and the live numbers are directly comparable.
Follow-up same day: STD_WINDOW_SIZE was dropped 100->50 (~0.5s) to cut
perceived UI latency. That broke presence reliability -- live `activity`
during real strong movement measured mean=0.32 (below MOVING_MIN=0.5),
vs mean=0.51 back at STD_WINDOW_SIZE=100. Likely cause: a 0.5s window is
shorter than a walking gait cycle (~1s), so it misses the natural
rhythmic variation in window_std that produces the `activity` signal --
not just noisier, systematically lower. Reverted to 100. If UI latency
needs cutting again, shrink CSI_WINDOW_SIZE (the *first* window,
currently 50/~0.5s) instead of STD_WINDOW_SIZE, or accept the ~1.5s.
Also added MOTION_SCALE (display ceiling, separate from MOVING_MIN the
presence threshold) and MOTION_GAMMA (power-curve applied to the
ratio) purely to shape the UI amplitude -- neither affects detection.
Measured at STD_WINDOW_SIZE=100 during real strong movement: activity
mean=0.51, std=0.38, max=1.92. Set MOTION_SCALE=1.0 (roughly mean +
1.3*std) and MOTION_GAMMA=2.0 from that reading; user confirmed the
result looked right live. If tuning again, remember MOTION_SCALE only
makes sense measured at whatever STD_WINDOW_SIZE is currently set --
changing the window changes activity's scale, which was the whole
source of the confusion above.
IMPORTANT, same evening ~17:00-20:00: node 1's empty-room baseline drifted
from window_std~8.9/activity~0.1 (afternoon) to window_std~38-39/
activity mean=0.42 max=1.65 (evening), completely unprompted -- no code
change, no furniture, node 2 unplugged and ruled out as a cause (baseline
identical with/without it running), LED sending ruled out too (identical
with LED_NODE_IDS emptied). Best working theory: ambient WiFi congestion
varies by time of day (neighbors' networks, more household devices active
in the evening) and the channel simply got noisier -- not a bug, not
movement, not anything in this repo. The empty vs moving CONTRAST held up
(~5.6x both before and after: moving mean=2.35 max=10.27 that evening),
so the metric itself is still sound -- only the absolute scale shifts.
This means static per-node thresholds are NOT robust across a full day/
night cycle at this location. A real fix needs an adaptive baseline
(e.g. a slow-moving EMA of `activity` itself, comparing recent readings
against it rather than a fixed constant) -- not implemented yet. Until
then, expect to re-tune SPECTRUM_MOVING_MIN/LED_MIN/MOTION_SCALE by
time of day, the same way this file now has two very different sets of
'right' numbers for the same node less than a day apart.
